A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraceGrad research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original TraceGrad experiments on eight Hamiltonian benchmarks, downstream physical-quantity predictions, and component ablations in Appendix F.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds DFT convergence results, inference-time measurements, and a HarmoSE-based experiment.

M1.justification: V4 Section 5.1 expands the invariant construction into multiple channels, sums their gradients, and feeds invariant features from all encoder layers into the trace decoder; v3 Section 6.1 specifies a scalar construction and final-layer decoder input. The prescribed losses also change: v3 uses MSE for both targets, whereas v4 uses MAE for trace prediction and combined MSE/MAE for QH9 Hamiltonians. These materially revise the described architecture and objective while retaining the TraceGrad principle.

E1.justification: The eight databases and their thermal-motion, twist, size-extrapolation, and trajectory scenarios are retained. V4 adds the downstream task of using predicted Hamiltonians to initialize DFT convergence on 50 molecules (Table 3). The HarmoSE case study uses the existing Monolayer MoS2 dataset.

E2.justification: DeepH-E3 and QHNet remain the principal comparators. V4 Table 8 adds quantitative comparisons with HarmoSE and DeepH-2 on Monolayer MoS2; these works were already cited in v3 but were not evaluated as comparators there. The new DFT evaluation also includes 1e and minao initialization references.

E3.justification: V4 Appendix F changes the stated QH9 training batch size from 16 to 32 and lambda from 0.3 to 0.2. It also introduces a 50-molecule PySCF convergence protocol with achieved/error-level ratios and a batch-size-one GPU timing protocol. Dataset splits remain unchanged. These are substantial reported setting and evaluation-design changes, although the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original Trace-only and Grad-only ablations are retained. V4 adds analyses of inference overhead on four datasets (Appendix I) and a case study testing whether TraceGrad benefits an approximately equivariant HarmoSE backbone (Appendix J). These substantially extend the analysis to computational cost and compatibility beyond strictly equivariant backbones.

E5.justification: The principal accuracy experiments still report ten repetitions. V4 clarifies that seeds match the respective backbone implementations, reports per-condition means and standard deviations across 50 molecules in Table 3, and specifies 50 timing repetitions per sample. No increase in the principal training-run count is established.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation table values are unchanged. V4 adds substantial results: Table 3 reports QS/1e achieved ratios of 0.400 ± 0.030 for QHNet and 0.345 ± 0.038 for QHNet+TraceGrad; Appendix I reports MG inference times of 0.247 and 0.264 seconds/sample for DeepH-E3 and its TraceGrad extension; Table 8 reports MM average MAEs of 0.21, 0.233, and 0.178 meV for DeepH-2, HarmoSE, and HarmoSE+TraceGrad. The reported QH9 repeat-run SD bound also changes from 0.007 to 0.009 meV.

T1.justification: The two central theorems and their proofs remain mathematically unchanged. V4 Appendix A adds formal definitions of groups, representations, equivariance, and invariance. Appendix I additionally develops the scaling argument by distinguishing quadratic pair counts in small dense systems from asymptotically linear counts under a fixed cutoff.

C1.justification: The central trace-supervision/gradient-induction contribution and the headline accuracy improvements of up to 40% and 76% are retained. V4 adds a prominent claim of improved DFT convergence acceleration in its abstract, introduction, and new conclusion, extending the claimed practical contribution.

C2.justification: V4 explains that applications requiring especially high numerical precision may still require DFT, with learned Hamiltonians serving as initializations. It also interprets the measured inference overhead as an acceptable accuracy tradeoff and the HarmoSE experiment as evidence of broader compatibility. The existing explanation of Trace/Grad complementarity is retained and relocated.

D1.justification: V3's brief training appendix expands into detailed implementation information in v4 Appendices D–F: GPU hardware, PyTorch versions, encoder depths, placement on edge features, invariant-channel and decoder dimensions, lambda search ranges, and learning-rate schedules including warm-up. V4 also adds a QHNet backbone-code link. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation, although v3's explicit instruction about omitting the invariant decoder during inference is not retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references to PySCF and Wang et al.'s universal materials Hamiltonian model, develops its relationship to the already-cited HarmoSE work, and removes several references including KAN and vision surveys. Much of the new main-text Related Work section reworks v3 Appendix A, so relocation does not represent an entirely new literature review.

P1.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes the narrative: methods precede experiments, related work moves into the main text, and future work and complexity discussion move to appendices. It adds a conclusion, ethics statement, and background section, rewrites explanatory passages, and revises front matter, including removing Feng Wu from the author list. A new Section 6.1 summary sentence mistakenly reverses the mol/ood descriptions, although the detailed split descriptions remain correct.

P2.justification: V4 adopts an ICLR layout and substantially rearranges displays. V3 Tables 1–2 and 3–4 become merged v4 Tables 1 and 2; DFT Table 3 and HarmoSE Table 8/Figure 7 are added. The framework diagram shows channel-summed gradients, and the Hamiltonian illustration is redrawn and moved to the appendix. The representative main-text block-error panel is removed while its results remain in the appendix; existing plot annotations are repositioned without changing their values.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses important gaps in practical validation and reproducibility: Table 3 and Appendix I provide DFT convergence and inference-overhead evidence absent from v3, while Appendices D–F specify the architecture and training much more concretely. The HarmoSE case study adds a useful check of broader applicability. These gains substantially strengthen the paper despite localized wording errors, including the reversed mol/ood summary. The original accuracy tables remain unchanged, so the improvement rests on stronger documentation and validation.
